# AI Resources Book Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A Starlight site shaped like a book (parts → chapters, as hidden drafts for now) plus a typed, interlinked library of resources, deployed to GitHub Pages.

**Architecture:** Astro + Starlight builds a static site. Chapters are MDX in the `docs` collection, with one folder per part and an autogenerated sidebar. Library entries are YAML files in a separate `library` collection whose schema references `docs` entries. Pure helpers in `src/lib/library.ts` do grouping, filtering and base-path joining. They're unit-tested with `bun test` and used by the library pages and by a `MarkdownContent` override that appends "Further reading" to chapters.

**Tech Stack:** Bun 1.4, Astro 7.4, @astrojs/starlight 0.42, astro-mermaid 2.2 + mermaid 12, GitHub Actions (`withastro/action`) → GitHub Pages.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-ai-resources-book-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Bun is the package manager and script runner. No npm/pnpm lockfiles.
- `site: 'https://tcorzo.github.io'`, `base: '/ai-resources'`, set once in `astro.config.mjs`. Every internal link must respect `base`.
- **Write no prose content.** Chapter stubs have only frontmatter (`title`, `draft: true`, `sidebar.order`) and no body. Library entries have no `note`. The home page holds only structure (title and links), with no explanatory copy.
- `CLAUDE.md` must not restrict agents from writing prose.
- Library `note` is optional. Agents adding entries ask the author for the note instead of inventing one.
- Code examples aren't run or tested. Don't add a Python toolchain.
- Default Starlight styling. No theme work.

## Review Focus

1. **Library entry referencing a chapter that doesn't exist.** The build must fail with a message naming the entry. Verified in Task 2, Step 5.
2. **Entry referencing only draft chapters.** The production site lists the item but renders no link to the hidden chapter, so there are no 404s. Tested by `publishedChapters` in Task 3 and the dist check in Task 4.
3. **Links under `/ai-resources/`.** Library, tag and further-reading links must all carry the base. Tested by `withBase` in Task 3 and the dist check in Task 4.
4. **Chapter with no linked items.** It gets no empty "Further reading" heading. Tested in Task 4.
5. **Tags with caps or spaces** would give inconsistent tag URLs. The schema enforces `^[a-z0-9-]+$`. Verified in Task 2, Step 5.

### Task 2: Library collection and seed entries

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/content.config.ts`
- Create: `src/content/library/<id>.yaml` × 17

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: docs ids from Task 1.
- Produces: collection `library`. Entry `id` = file name without extension. Data fields:
  - `title: string`
  - `url: string (url)`
  - `type: 'article' | 'talk' | 'interview' | 'paper' | 'model' | 'tool' | 'repo' | 'newsletter' | 'inspiration'`
  - `creator: string`
  - `summary: string`: one factual line describing what the resource is, taken from its own page. This is not the author's opinion.
  - `published?: date`: for articles, talks and model releases
  - `links: { label: string; url: string (url) }[]` (default `[]`): secondary links such as weights, docs, a playground or a benchmark
  - `tags: string[]` (each matches `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/`; default `[]`)
  - `note?: string`: the author's own "why it's worth your time"
  - `chapters: reference('docs')[]` (default `[]`)
  - `related: reference('library')[]` (default `[]`)
  - `added: date`

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the `library` collection.** Use `glob({ pattern: '**/*.yaml', base: './src/content/library' })` and the schema above (`z` from `astro/zod`, `reference` from `astro:content`). Export it alongside `docs`.

### Task 3: Library helpers and library pages

**Files:**
- Create: `src/lib/library.ts`, `src/lib/library.test.ts`
- Create: `src/components/LibraryItem.astro`
- Create: `src/pages/library/index.astro`, `src/pages/library/tags/[tag].astro`
- Modify: `package.json` (`"test": "bun test src"`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `library` and `docs` collections.
- Produces, in `src/lib/library.ts` (plain TS, no `astro:content` import, so it's testable):
  - `type Ref = { id: string }`
  - `type Item = { id: string; data: { title: string; type: string; tags: string[]; chapters: Ref[]; related: Ref[] } }`
  - `TYPE_ORDER: readonly string[]`, in the schema enum order
  - `TYPE_LABELS: Record<string, string>` (`article → 'Articles'`, … `inspiration → 'Inspiration'`)
  - `withBase(base: string, path: string): string`
  - `groupByType<T extends Item>(items: T[]): Array<{ type: string; items: T[] }>`, in `TYPE_ORDER`, with empty groups omitted and items sorted by title
  - `allTags(items: Item[]): string[]`, unique and sorted
  - `itemsForChapter<T extends Item>(items: T[], chapterId: string): T[]`, sorted by title
  - `publishedChapters(refs: Ref[], published: Set<string>): Ref[]`
- `LibraryItem.astro` props: `{ item: CollectionEntry<'library'>; published: Set<string>; titles: Map<string, string> }`. It renders the title linked to `url`, creator, type, `published` (if present), `summary`, secondary `links` as small labelled links, tags (linked to tag pages), the note if present (visually distinct from `summary`, since it's the author's voice), and "Cited in:" links to published chapters only (omitted when there are none).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests** in `src/lib/library.test.ts`:
  - `withBase('/ai-resources', '/library/')` → `'/ai-resources/library/'`. The same for base `'/ai-resources/'` and path `'library/'`. `withBase('/', '/library/')` → `'/library/'`.
  - `groupByType` on `[tool "B", article "Z", tool "A"]` → `[{type:'article',…[Z]}, {type:'tool',…[A,B]}]`.
  - `allTags` on items with tags `[evals, agents]` and `[evals]` → `['agents','evals']`.
  - `itemsForChapter(items, 'part-3-building-and-judging/evals')` returns only items whose `chapters` include that id, sorted by title, and `[]` when none do.
  - `publishedChapters([{id:'a'},{id:'b'}], new Set(['b']))` → `[{id:'b'}]`.

### Task 4: "Further reading" on chapters and dist checks

**Files:**
- Create: `src/components/MarkdownContent.astro` (Starlight override), `src/components/FurtherReading.astro`
- Modify: `astro.config.mjs` (`components: { MarkdownContent: './src/components/MarkdownContent.astro' }`)
- Create: `tests/dist.test.ts`
- Modify: `package.json` (`"test:dist": "bun run build && bun test tests"`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `itemsForChapter`, `withBase`, `LibraryItem` from Task 3.
- `MarkdownContent.astro` renders Starlight's default `@astrojs/starlight/components/MarkdownContent.astro` with `<slot />`. Then, for docs routes (`Astro.locals.starlightRoute.entry.id`), it renders `<FurtherReading chapterId={id} />`.
- `FurtherReading.astro` renders nothing when `itemsForChapter` is empty. Otherwise it renders `<h2>Further reading</h2>` and the item list, each item with its note when present.
